LETTER 65
Efficient Synthesis of 2,3-Dihydrofurans via the Highly Selective Pd(0)-
Catalyzed Coupling-Cyclization Reaction of 3,4-Allenols with Aryl Iodides
Effi ci ent Synthesis of 2,3-Di hydrofuransShengming Ma,* Wenzhong Gao
State Key Laboratory of Organometallic Chemistry, Shanghai Institute of Organic Chemistry, Chinese Academy of Sciences, 354 Fenglin 
Lu, Shanghai 200032, P. R. China
Fax +86(21)64166128; E-mail: masm@pub.sioc.ac.cn
Received 25 September 2001
Synlett 2002, No. 1, 28 12 2001. Article Identifier: 
1437-2096,E;2002,0,01,0065,0068,ftx,en;Y20201ST.pdf. 
© Georg Thieme Verlag Stuttgart · New York
ISSN 0936-5214
Abstract: Highly selective coupling-cyclization of 3,4-allenols
with aryl iodides via the oxidative addition- exo-mode oxypallada-
tion-reductive elimination sequence afforded 2,3-dihydrofurans ef-
ficiently. The cyclization mode and the regioselectivity observed
for 3,4-allenols are unique and different from what was reported
previously.
Key words: alcohols, allenes, furans, palladium, cyclizations
Furans and dihydrofurans are not only widely present in
natural products and non-natural compounds of pharma-
ceutical and agrochemical interest,
1,2 but are also versatile
intermediates in organic synthesis.3 Thus, much attention
has been paid to the development of new methodologies
for the synthesis of furans and dihydrofurans. 4 2,3-Dihy-
drofurans can be prepared from a two-step procedure from
/c103-butyrolactone,5 base promoted cycloisomerization of
3,4-allenols,6 and conjugate addition of 3,4-epoxy-2-me-
thylene oxolanes, 7 intramolecular enolate addition to 1-
alkenyl sulfones,8 base-mediated nucleophilic cyclization
of 5,5-difluoro-4-enols,9 addition reaction of 1,3-dicarbo-
nyl compounds with alkenes,10 transition metal-catalyzed
coupling-cyclization of /c97-diazoketones with ethyl vinyl
ether,11 Pd-catalyzed cyclization of silyl-substituted
bis(homo)propargylic alcohols, 12 Cr-mediated cycloi-
somerization of  homopropargyl  alcohols, 13 and the re-
action of p-TolSO2Na with 1-hydoxybut-3-
ynyl(phenyl)iodium triflate derivatives. 14 For all these
methods, some of them require lengthy procedure, some
need stoichiometric amount of metal complexes. Thus,
the development of new and efficient methods for the syn-
thesis of 2,3-dihydrofurans is still catching the attention of
synthetic chemists. Recently, during the course of our
studies of cyclization of functionalized allenes,
15,16 we
have developed some new methodologies for the efficient
synthesis of vinylic oxiranes,
17 and furans 18,19 starting
from 2,3-allenols or 1,2-allenyl ketones. In this letter, we
wish to communicate our recent observation on the Pd(0)-
catalyzed coupling-cyclization reaction of 3,4-allenols
with aryl iodides via the oxidative addition-exo-mode ox-
ypalladation-reductive elimination sequence affording
2,3-dihydrofurans (Scheme).
During the course of our study of Pd(0)-catalyzed cou-
pling-cyclization reaction of 2,3-allenols, we observed the
exclusive formation of vinylic epoxides via either the car-
bopalladation of allenes followed by the intramolecular
nucleophilic trapping of the in situ formed 
/c112-allyl palladi-
um species (n = 0, pathway 1b, Scheme) or the Pd(II)-me-
diated exo-mode oxypalladation-reductive elimination
(pathway 2, Scheme). 17 In principle, the possibility of
forming 2,3-dihydrofurans ( n = 1) exists, although we
have not observed this pathway so far (pathway 3a,
Scheme). Recently, when we switched from the chemistry
of 2,3-allenols to that of 3,4-allenols, to our surprise, the
exclusive formation of 2,3-dihydrofuran 2a in 56% yield
via Pd(PPh
3)4-catalyzed coupling-cyclization reaction of
2-methyl-3-butyl-penta-3,4-dienol ( 1a) with PhI was ob-
served (Equation and entry 3 of Table 1). It should be not-
ed that the Lewis acid-catalyzed cyclization of 3,4-
allenols afforded pyran derivatives.
20
After careful examination of the crude reaction mixture,
we found that the 6-membered product 3a (n = 1, pathway

1a or pathway 3b, Scheme) and 4-membered product 4a
(n = 1, pathway 1b and pathway 2, Scheme) were not
formed. From Table 1, the following points are notewor-
thy: (1) The reaction did not afford 2a in decent yields in
toluene using K
2CO3 and n-Bu4NBr as the base (entry 1,
Table 1) or in DMF using Na 2CO3 as the base (entry 2,
Table 1); (2) The cation of the inorganic base has a very
big impact on this reaction (compare entries 2, 3 and 5,
Table 1); (3) The addition of n-Bu
4NBr has some influ-
ence for this reaction when the reaction was carried in
CH
3CN using K 2CO3 as the base (compare entry 8 with
entry 9 of Table 1). Thus, we used 5 mol% Pd(PPh 3)4,
Cs2CO3 (4 equiv.) and DMF as the standard reaction con-
ditions.
Some typical results of the Pd(0)-catalyzed reaction of 2-
methyl-3-butyl-penta-3,4-dienol ( 1a) with differently
substituted aryl halides are summarized in Table 2. The
following points are noteworthy (1) For aryl halides with
different carbon-halogen bonds, only the carbon-iodine
bond was cleaved (entries 1–3, Table 2); (2) Both elec-
tron-donating and electron-withdrawing aryl iodides can
be reacted to afford the corresponding products (entries 4–
9, Table 2).
The scope of 3,4-allenols is summarized in Table 3. Based
on the results in Table 3, it can be conduced that (1) a sub-
stituent at 3-position in 3,4-allenols is necessary since no
expected cyclization products were obtained with 3-un-
substituted 3,4-allenols 1g and 1h.; (2) the substiuents at
1, 2 or 5-positions in 3,4-allenols are quite flexible.
In conclusion, we have developed an efficient synthesis of
2,3-dihydrofurans starting from the easily available 3,4-
allenols.
21 Based on the structure of the products, it can be
concluded that the reaction proceeds via a highly selective
oxidative addition- exo-mode oxypalladation of the C-C
double bond at 4-position-reductive elimination reaction,
which is quite different from what we observed in our pre-
vious studies.
16–19 Further studies on this reaction includ-
ing the factors controlling the reactivities of 3,4-allenols,
the scope, and the synthetic application are being carried
out in our laboratory.
